title: supaya, biar — so that
pattern: A supaya B · A biar B
explanation: supaya gives the purpose, looking ahead to what you want to happen: Saya berangkat pagi supaya tidak terlambat. — I'm leaving early so I won't be late. The purpose part can have its own subject: Tolong bicara pelan-pelan supaya saya mengerti. agar means the same and is more formal, and biar is the casual one, very common among friends: Kita berangkat sekarang biar nggak kena macet. For a simple to + verb with the same subject, untuk also works: Saya ke Jakarta untuk kerja.
natural: supaya in everyday polite speech, biar with friends and family, agar on signs, in instructions and in speeches.
stiff: agar in a chat sounds like a notice on the wall, and biar to an official can sound too casual. Careful too: biar also means let, as in Biar saya yang bayar — Let me pay.

examples.indonesian: Saya berangkat pagi supaya tidak terlambat.
examples.english: I'm leaving early so I won't be late.

gap.why: supaya looks ahead to what you want, not being late; karena would give a reason that's already true.

examples.indonesian: Tolong bicara pelan-pelan supaya saya mengerti.
examples.english: Please speak slowly so I can understand.

gap.why: Understanding is what you want to happen: supaya, so that.

examples.indonesian: Minum air putih yang banyak supaya cepat sembuh.
examples.english: Drink plenty of water so you get better soon.

gap.note: agar means the same but is the formal one: it sounds like a leaflet from the clinic.
gap.why: Getting better is the goal of drinking the water: supaya.

examples.indonesian: Kita berangkat sekarang biar nggak kena macet.
examples.english: Let's leave now so we don't get stuck in traffic.

gap.note: supaya works too; biar is what you'd say to friends.
gap.why: biar is the casual so that; soalnya would give a reason, not a goal.
